label: Unstructured Data and Cortex
topic: Data Transformation: unstructured data and semantic views

questions.scenario: A provider shares a secure view over a directory table so that a consumer account can open contract PDFs from an internal stage. The view returns the FILE_URL column of the directory table. Consumers query the view but cannot open any of the files. The provider requires that each consumer authenticates to Snowflake to reach a file, and that no link works for anyone who just holds it.
questions.stem: Which change to the view meets the requirement?

options.text: Return BUILD_STAGE_FILE_URL(@contracts, relative_path) instead of FILE_URL
Return GET_PRESIGNED_URL(@contracts, relative_path, 60) instead of FILE_URL
Return BUILD_SCOPED_FILE_URL(@contracts, relative_path) instead of FILE_URL
Run ALTER STAGE contracts REFRESH so that FILE_URL values are regenerated for consumers

explanation.correct: File URLs can't be accessed through a secure view in a share. A scoped URL does work through a share, is created when the consumer queries the view, and can be used only by the user who generated it, so it needs a Snowflake identity.

distractors.A: BUILD_STAGE_FILE_URL builds a file URL, the same URL type that fails in a shared secure view.
distractors.B: A pre-signed URL works through a share, but anyone holding it can open the file without a Snowflake login, which the provider ruled out.
distractors.D: REFRESH only updates the directory table's file metadata. It does not change which URL type the consumer can use.

questions.scenario: A team created an internal stage with default settings and enabled a directory table. A BI tool opens files through URLs from GET_PRESIGNED_URL, with report users who have no Snowflake login. The downloaded files are corrupt and will not open.

options.text: Run ALTER STAGE SET ENCRYPTION = (TYPE = 'SNOWFLAKE_SSE') on the existing stage
Recreate the stage with ENCRYPTION = (TYPE = 'SNOWFLAKE_SSE') and load the files again
Pass a longer expiration_time to GET_PRESIGNED_URL
Replace the pre-signed URLs with scoped URLs from BUILD_SCOPED_FILE_URL

explanation.correct: Pre-signed URLs on an internal stage need server-side encryption (SNOWFLAKE_SSE). A stage created without it returns corrupt files, and the encryption type of a stage can't be changed, so the stage has to be recreated.

distractors.A: The encryption type of an existing stage can't be changed.
distractors.C: Expiry controls how long the URL stays valid. It has no effect on whether the downloaded file is readable.
distractors.D: A scoped URL can be used only by the user who generated it, so report users without a Snowflake login couldn't open it.

questions.scenario: An external stage on Amazon S3 has a directory table but no AUTO_REFRESH. The stage holds several million files and grows all day. A nightly job drops files under the prefix 2024/01/31/, and SELECT * FROM DIRECTORY(@landing) does not list them. The Engineer wants them registered at the lowest cost.
questions.stem: Which statement should the Engineer run?

options.text: GRANT SELECT ON DIRECTORY(@landing) TO ROLE etl_role
ALTER STAGE landing SET DIRECTORY = (ENABLE = TRUE)
ALTER STAGE landing REFRESH
ALTER STAGE landing REFRESH SUBPATH = '2024/01/31'

explanation.correct: A directory table is updated only by a refresh when auto-refresh is off. A manual refresh performs a list operation, which is slow and costly on big stages. REFRESH SUBPATH narrows the listing to the new prefix.

distractors.A: A directory table has no grantable privileges of its own, and the problem is stale metadata, not access.
distractors.B: The directory table is already enabled. Enabling it again doesn't register the new files.
distractors.C: This would register the files, but it lists the whole stage. That is the cost the Engineer is trying to avoid.

questions.scenario: A Java UDTF reads PDF files from an internal stage and returns the extracted text. The owner role will expose it to many other roles. A security review warns that a caller could supply an arbitrary stage path and read files they should not see.
questions.stem: How should the function receive the file location?

options.text: As a scoped URL built by the caller with BUILD_SCOPED_FILE_URL
As a VARCHAR stage path that the handler appends to the stage name
As a pre-signed URL built with GET_PRESIGNED_URL
As a file URL taken from the FILE_URL column of the directory table

explanation.correct: Passing a scoped URL protects the handler against file injection. This matters whenever the caller is not the function's owner, because a scoped URL is tied to the user who generated it and can't be pointed at an arbitrary file.

distractors.B: A free-form path lets the caller choose any file the owner's rights can read, which is the file injection risk.
distractors.C: A pre-signed URL is valid for anyone who holds it, so it does not tie access to the caller.
distractors.D: A file URL is permanent and not tied to the user who generated it. It gives no protection against file injection.

questions.scenario: A data team creates a semantic view named sales_sv over several tables. An analyst role has USAGE on the database and schema, but no privileges on the underlying tables. The analyst runs SELECT * FROM SEMANTIC_VIEW(sales_sv DIMENSIONS customer.segment METRICS orders.total_revenue) and gets an insufficient privileges error.
questions.stem: Which grant lets the analyst run the query with the least access?

options.text: SELECT on each underlying table
SELECT on the semantic view
CREATE SEMANTIC VIEW on the schema
SELECT on the semantic view and on each underlying table

explanation.correct: A role that doesn't own the semantic view needs only SELECT on the semantic view itself, as with a standard view. It does not need privileges on the underlying tables.

distractors.A: Privileges on the tables alone don't give access to the semantic view, and they expose more data than needed.
distractors.C: CREATE SEMANTIC VIEW is needed to create the view. It doesn't allow querying it.
distractors.D: Table privileges are not needed to query a semantic view, so this grants more than is required.

questions.scenario: A loader role works with an internal stage that has a directory table. The role must list the staged files with SELECT * FROM DIRECTORY(@docs) and upload new files with PUT. The security team wants the role to have only the stage privileges the work needs.
questions.stem: Which TWO privileges on the stage does the role need?

options.text: USAGE
SELECT on the directory table
READ
OWNERSHIP
WRITE

explanation.correct: Querying a directory table on an internal stage needs READ on the stage, and PUT to an internal stage needs WRITE.

distractors.A: USAGE is the privilege for external stages. An internal stage uses READ and WRITE.
distractors.B: A directory table is an implicit object layered on a stage and has no grantable privileges of its own.
distractors.D: OWNERSHIP gives far more than the work needs, which breaks the least-privilege requirement.

questions.scenario: A reporting team builds links with GET_PRESIGNED_URL on an Amazon S3 external stage whose storage integration uses AWS_ROLE. Some users open links that show a NoSuchKey error. The team also wants links that stay valid for 3 days.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about GET_PRESIGNED_URL apply?

options.text: The default expiration is 604800 seconds
The function returns a URL even when the file does not exist, so a bad path shows as NoSuchKey in the browser
The URLs are permanent unless the file is removed
With an AWS_ROLE stage the maximum expiration is 3600 seconds, so a 3-day link is not possible
On Azure the function works with a SAS token, with no storage integration needed

explanation.correct: GET_PRESIGNED_URL doesn't check that the file exists. It returns a URL, and the error appears when the URL is opened. For a stage that uses AWS_ROLE the maximum expiration is 3600 seconds, even though the general maximum is 604800.

distractors.A: The default expiration is 3600 seconds. 604800 (7 days) is the maximum for stages that allow it.
distractors.C: Pre-signed URLs expire at the expiration time. Permanent URLs are file URLs.
distractors.E: On Azure the function needs a storage integration, not a SAS token.

questions.scenario: A team designs a semantic view over customers and orders tables. The design needs: the amount of each individual sale, total revenue as SUM of that amount, the customer market segment for grouping and filtering, and a link between orders and customers on the customer key.
questions.stem: Which THREE mappings to semantic view parts are correct?

options.text: The amount of each individual sale is a fact
Total revenue is a dimension
The customer market segment is a metric
The link between orders and customers is a relationship
The customer market segment is a dimension

explanation.correct: Facts are row-level numeric attributes, relationships join logical tables on shared keys, and dimensions are categorical attributes for grouping and filtering.

distractors.B: Total revenue is an aggregation of a fact, which makes it a metric.
distractors.C: A market segment is a categorical attribute used to group and filter, which makes it a dimension. Metrics are aggregations.

questions.scenario: An administrator limits Cortex AI usage per user. SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER was revoked from PUBLIC and granted only to a custom role AI_FUNCTIONS_USER_ROLE. A budget table records each user's allowance. An hourly task revokes that role from users who exceed their budget, and a monthly task restores it. Several over-budget users still run AI functions every day.
questions.stem: What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The monthly task restores the role before the month ends
Those users hold SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER through another role
The warehouse is larger than MEDIUM
SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER can't be revoked once it has been granted to PUBLIC

explanation.correct: The limit works by removing the one custom role that carries CORTEX_USER. A user whose other role also includes CORTEX_USER keeps access when the custom role is revoked, so any other role that includes it bypasses the limit.

distractors.A: The monthly task restores the role at the month change. It doesn't explain access continuing during the month.
distractors.C: Warehouse size affects cost, with no gain in speed above MEDIUM. It has no link to who can call the functions.
distractors.D: CORTEX_USER can be revoked from PUBLIC. That revoke is the first step of the per-user limit design.

questions.scenario: A pipeline runs AI_EXTRACT over contracts on a stage. Files are up to 400 pages and all pages must be read. The account does not have cross-region inference enabled, and each run fails when a file has more than 125 pages. One bad file should not stop the statement either.

options.text: Enable cross-region inference
Set scale_factor to 4.0
Pass FL_FILTER_PAGES so that only the first 125 pages are extracted
Move the query to a warehouse larger than MEDIUM

explanation.correct: With cross-region inference the page limit is 1,000, and a file that can't be processed sets the error field for that file while the statement continues. Without it the limit is 125 pages and a failing file fails the statement.

distractors.B: scale_factor applies only when cross-region inference is not used, and it doesn't raise the page limit.
distractors.C: This keeps the statement running, but it drops the pages after 125, and the task needs all pages.
distractors.D: Warehouse size doesn't change the page limit. A warehouse larger than MEDIUM costs more with no speed gain.

questions.scenario: A team runs AI_CLASSIFY on 5 million support tickets with 8 categories. To improve accuracy they add a description to every category and a set of few-shot examples. Accuracy improves, but the credit cost per run rises sharply even though the ticket text is unchanged.

options.text: The descriptions and examples are billed once per call, and the added cost comes from output tokens
The category descriptions are billed per page, like AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT
The descriptions and examples count as input tokens, and they are billed for every record
The function adds a fixed charge for each category beyond the first two

explanation.correct: Category labels, descriptions and examples count as input tokens for every record, not once per call. Across 5 million rows the added tokens multiply.

distractors.A: The extra text is input, and it is billed for every record, not once per call.
distractors.B: Per-page billing applies to AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT. AI_CLASSIFY is billed on input and output tokens.
distractors.D: AI_CLASSIFY is billed on tokens. It has no per-category charge, though more than twenty categories can reduce accuracy.

questions.scenario: An Engineer calls AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT on 40-page PDF reports. Only pages 5 to 9 (as people count them) are needed, and the embedded images must be extracted too.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about the function's options are correct?

options.text: The default mode is LAYOUT
extract_images needs the LAYOUT mode
page_filter uses zero-based pages with the end page inclusive
page_filter can safely be combined with FL_FILTER_PAGES
page_filter implies page_split

explanation.correct: extract_images works only in LAYOUT mode, so the default OCR mode isn't enough. page_filter implies page_split, so page splitting does not need to be turned on separately.

distractors.A: The default mode is OCR, which returns text only.
distractors.C: page_filter is zero-based with an inclusive start and an exclusive end, so pages 5 to 9 need the range 4 to 9.
distractors.D: page_filter should not be combined with FL_FILTER_PAGES.

questions.scenario: A backend service for a customer chat feature needs low-latency LLM responses. A developer proposes calling AI functions in SQL for every message. The platform team also needs to track the usage and credits of the calls.

options.text: For interactive, low-latency use the Cortex REST API is the better fit than SQL AI functions
The /api/v2/cortex/v1/messages endpoint serves models from every provider
The Cortex REST API authenticates with a programmatic access token
CORTEX_AI_FUNCTIONS_USAGE_HISTORY holds the REST API requests and credits
The /api/v2/cortex/v1/responses endpoint is generally available for all models on every cloud

explanation.correct: AI functions in SQL are built for throughput on large tables, and the Cortex REST API is for low-latency use. The Cortex REST API authenticates with a programmatic access token (PAT).

distractors.B: The messages endpoint is Anthropic-compatible and serves Claude models only.
distractors.D: REST API requests are tracked in CORTEX_REST_API_USAGE_HISTORY. The SQL function views have no granular data for them.
distractors.E: The responses endpoint is in preview and serves OpenAI models on AWS only.
